brief: A caddy for next to my kitchen sink: a dispenser that pours out bleach for wiping the counters, plus two bins for sponges.

requirements.requirement: A caddy for next to the kitchen sink (one joined unit)
requirements.evidence: Three full cells in a row (piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) as one body, joints bolted (lockJoints) and open faces capped (capOpenFaces). check_build: one group, meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: A dispenser that pours out bleach for wiping counters
requirements.evidence: No part or prop in the catalog dispenses or pours liquid (find_parts 'dispenser bottle pour' = 0; no spout/pump fitting offered). The centre cell (piece:0,0,0 with solid top cover cover:0,0,0;full;top) is at most a closed placeholder reservoir position, not a pouring dispenser. Also unmet on safety/material grounds: the configurator checks fit only and knows nothing about chemical resistance, so a 3D-printed part cannot be shown safe to store or pour bleach. Use a purpose-made, bleach-rated dispenser bottle and stand it beside/in this caddy instead.
Two full-depth drained bins: bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, one at each end of the caddy; drained floors suit wet sponges next to a sink.

finish.summary: Built a safe part of the brief: a three-cell sink-side caddy with two full-depth drained sponge bins (one at each end). The centre cell is a lidded placeholder where a dispenser would sit, but the bleach-pouring dispenser itself is unmet: no catalog part pours/dispenses liquid, and bleach compatibility of printed plastic cannot be verified here — use a commercial bleach-rated dispenser bottle with this caddy. Parts settled, open faces capped, joints locked, check_build clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Building your sink-side caddy — a bleach pourer shape plus two sponge bins. I'll check what dispenser parts exist, noting printed plastic can't be certified for bleach.
